description:
## Intent

v0.4's headline: upgrade the menubar dropdown from the v0.3 NSMenu (T-014) to a rich NSPopover+SwiftUI surface — while retiring the last UI-side carried-unverified flag from the plan (`product-architecture-2026-07-30.md`, "Carried unverified flags": *"NSPopover bundle-less → v0.4 start"*).

**FIRST: de-risk NSPopover+SwiftUI in the raw bundle-less binary.** The plan's UI section is explicit: *"v0.4 NSPopover+SwiftUI (unverified bundle-less — de-risk first)"*. The proven prototype is a 112 KB bundle-less Swift `NSStatusItem` helper (~45 MB RSS, stdio JSON-lines IPC); whether NSPopover hosting SwiftUI content works from a bare executable with no `.app` bundle has never been verified. If the spike fails, an explicit decision is required — **flat-.app pull-forward vs NSMenu-only for v0.4** — and that decision interacts with D4/T-016 (notarization tickets don't staple to bare executables, so a failed spike here and a signing need there both push toward the flat `.app`, which is otherwise T-021/v0.5 scope).

## Scope

**In:**
- De-risk spike, day 1 of the phase (plan risk #6: prototype-gated design points are scheduled day-1 so failure re-plans early, not late): show an NSPopover with SwiftUI content from the NSStatusItem in the raw bundle-less binary; record the outcome.
- If the spike passes: the full rich popover layout, mirroring the v1 NSMenu information architecture (plan, UI section): **header (today / week / Δ) → burn strip (active block) → Claude-vs-Codex + model split bars → top-5 projects with combined $ and sparklines**.
- Data comes from the service snapshot over the existing stdio JSON-lines IPC (helper stays a view; service remains sole writer).

**Out:** settings surface, health dot, stale greying, update line (T-020); notifications / SMAppService / flat `.app` (T-021, unless the pull-forward decision is made); quota mode (T-022). Title/overflow contract and NSMenu itself are T-014 and must keep working.

## Approach notes

- The NSMenu dropdown from T-014 is the proven fallback; the spike failing degrades v0.4 to NSMenu-only rather than blocking the phase.
- Sparklines imply per-project time-series in the IPC payload — the snapshot schema has per-day data, but the plan does not specify sparkline window or payload shape (see open questions).
- Quality bar is owner-stated "robust, smooth, performant": watch RSS against the ~45 MB prototype baseline; deterministic perf checks are hard CI gates, wall-clock is baseline-comparison only (plan, Quality bar rulings).

## Constraints

- Helper stays in the npm tarball with CI-measured size; 1 MB packed threshold triggers the platform-split revisit (plan, Verdict architecture).
- `usage.py` is the frozen oracle — untouched. `package.json` never carries an author field. No real transcript data or personal paths in any fixture used for popover rendering tests.

## Acceptance criteria
1. A de-risk spike (run before any layout work) demonstrates an NSPopover presenting SwiftUI content from the NSStatusItem in the raw bundle-less helper binary (no .app bundle), with the outcome recorded; if it fails, a recorded decision exists choosing flat-.app pull-forward vs NSMenu-only, and the rest of this ticket is re-scoped accordingly
2. Popover renders all four sections from snapshot data delivered over the existing stdio JSON-lines IPC: header (today/week/Δ), burn strip for the active block, Claude-vs-Codex + model split bars, top-5 projects with combined $ and sparklines
3. The v0.3 NSMenu path (T-014) still works — the popover does not regress title modes, overflow contract, or menu actions (refresh / settings / Stop service / Quit menubar)
4. Universal-binary CI (both slices, lipo, declared MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET) stays green with the popover code included, and packed tarball size remains under the 1 MB revisit threshold or the revisit is explicitly triggered
5. No real transcript data or personal paths appear in any fixture or screenshot committed for this work

## Risks
The whole ticket rests on a carried-unverified flag: NSPopover+SwiftUI may simply not work from a bundle-less binary (SwiftUI hosting can require NSApplication/bundle machinery), forcing a re-plan whose two exits both cost something — flat-.app pull-forward pulls v0.5 packaging and the D4 signing question forward; NSMenu-only shrinks the v0.4 deliverable. Secondary: SwiftUI could bloat the 112 KB binary or the ~45 MB RSS profile against the owner's "robust, smooth, performant" bar.

## Open questions (owner decisions)
1. If the bundle-less spike fails: flat-.app pull-forward (drags T-021 scope into v0.4 and interacts with D4/T-016 cost decision) or NSMenu-only v0.4? Owner call.
2. Sparkline definition: time window (7d? 30d?), data granularity, and whether the IPC payload grows a per-project series field — plan is silent.
3. Does the popover replace the NSMenu dropdown outright, or do both coexist (e.g. right-click menu + left-click popover)? Plan is silent.
4. Acceptable RSS budget for the SwiftUI popover vs the ~45 MB prototype baseline — plan gives no number.
title: Rich popover: NSPopover/SwiftUI de-risk + full layout
